text: What did the kitchen look like in the home you grew up in? What's one detail you remember loving about it, or one you really disliked?
Which room do you spend the most time in? If I had to rebuild it from your description alone, what would I need to get right?
A friend is coming to your place for the first time and their phone is dead. Describe your street so they'd know they're on the right one.
You've got one free hour and perfect weather. Which outdoor spot near you do you head for, and what can you see from where you sit?
You're sending someone to your usual grocery store with a list of five things. Walk them through the store so they don't get lost.
Picture a classroom you sat in as a kid. Where was your seat, and what could you see from it?
If a stranger sat down at your desk or workspace right now, what would they figure out about you from what's on it?
You get to take one out-of-town guest to one restaurant or cafe near you. Where do you go, and what will they notice when they walk in?
Think of a station, bus stop or airport you know too well. What would you tell a first-timer to look out for there?
Think of a beach, lake or river you've been to more than once. Which spot on it would you claim as yours, and what does it look like?
Think of a relative's house you visited as a kid. What did it smell like, and which room were you not really supposed to go in?
You've got an afternoon to kill in a bookstore or library you know. Which corner do you end up in, and what's around you there?
Think of a gym, court or field where you've spent real time. What does it sound like, and what's the one thing about it that needs fixing?
What can you see from your bedroom window? If you could swap one thing in that view for anything else, what would you change?
Think of the last hotel or rental you stayed in. What would your honest review say about the room?
Think of a shop that sells basically one kind of thing: a key shop, a cheese shop, a guitar shop. What's it like inside, and who shops there?
What's the best venue you've ever seen a show in? Tell me what it looked like from where you were standing or sitting.
You're stuck in a waiting room for an hour with a dead phone. Think of a real one you've been in: what is there to look at?
Think of a playground you knew as a kid. Which piece of equipment did everyone fight over, and which one was actually dangerous?
You have $20 to spend at a street market or farmers market you know. Walk me past the stalls and tell me where the money goes.
Think of the place you get your hair cut. What do you look at while you're stuck in the chair?
Think of a garage, shed or closet where things go to be forgotten. What's in there, and what's the one thing you'd rescue?
A film crew wants to shoot one scene in your town or neighborhood. Which street or square do you send them to, and what will they see?
You can take one thing home from any museum you've visited, no questions asked. What do you take, and what does it look like up close?
Think of a trail, campsite or outdoor spot you'd go back to. What's the view when you get there, and what does it take to reach it?
What's the oldest thing you own? If it went missing, how would you describe it so someone could pick it out?
What's one piece of clothing you'd wear every day if nobody noticed? Describe it for me, including what shape it's in by now.
If I emptied the bag or pockets you carry every day onto a table, what would I find? Which item needs explaining?
Think of the car, bike or other ride you use most. If you were selling it tomorrow, what would the honest listing say?
Everyone has one mug, glass or bowl they reach for first. What does yours look like, and what makes it better than the others in the cupboard?
What toy from your childhood would you buy back today if you could? Tell me what it looked like and what it could do.
Which piece of furniture in your home has been through the most? Tell me what it looks like and where the damage is.
If you could wake up tomorrow able to play any instrument, which one? Describe it as if I've never seen one.
What's a tool or gadget you'd replace the same day if it broke? Tell me what it looks like and what you do with it.
What's a gift you've held on to for years? Describe it, and tell me where it lives now.
If I opened your refrigerator right now, what would I see? What's been in there the longest?
Which pair of your shoes has the most miles on it? Tell me what they look like now compared with the day you got them.
Think of a watch, ring or other piece that you or someone close to you wears every day. What does it look like, and where did it come from?
Which photo do you have out where people can see it? Tell me what's in the picture and what was happening just outside the frame.
What book or album cover can you picture without looking it up? Describe it well enough that I could find it on a shelf.
Without looking, what's on your phone's home screen? Which app has earned its spot, and which one should you have deleted by now?
What game comes out when people are over: a board game, cards, something else? Describe what's in the box for someone who's never played.
You can keep only one appliance in your kitchen. Which one survives, and what does it look and sound like when it's running?
Think of a tree or plant you know well: in a yard, on a street, on a windowsill. What does it look like at its best, and at its worst?
Think of a pet or an animal you see all the time. If it got loose, how would you describe it so a stranger could spot it?
What's hanging on your walls at home? Pick one thing and tell me what's in it and why it got the spot.
What do you put on when the weather is at its worst? Describe it, and tell me where it still lets the cold or the rain in.
Which light in your home do you switch on first when it gets dark? Tell me what it looks like and what it lights up.
Think of a remote, game controller or keyboard you use all the time. Which buttons are worn out, and which have you never once pressed?
Take me through your key ring, one item at a time. What does each key open, and what's on there that isn't a key?
Tell me about a trip that didn't go to plan. What went wrong first, and how did you get home?
Think back to your first day at a new job or school. What's the first thing you remember, and who was the first person you talked to?
What's the worst meal anyone has ever cooked for you? What was on the plate, and did you eat it anyway?
Tell me about the last time you lost something you really needed. Where did you look, and did it ever turn up?
Tell me about a time you got properly lost. Where were you trying to go, and how did you find your way back?
Tell me about a time a stranger did you a favor. What did they do, and what do you remember about them?
What's the best live event you've ever been to: a concert, a game, a show? What's the one moment from it you still think about?
Who taught you to drive, or to ride a bike? Tell me about the lesson that went the worst.
Tell me about a birthday you won't forget, yours or someone else's. What was the plan, and what actually happened?
Tell me about a time the weather wrecked your plans. What were you supposed to be doing, and what did you do instead?
Tell me about the day you moved into a place you've lived. What was the first night like, and what was the first thing to go wrong?
Tell me about a game that came down to the very end, one you played in or watched. What was riding on it, and how did it finish?
When did a piece of technology last fail you at the worst possible moment? What were you in the middle of, and how did you recover?
Think of someone important to you who isn't family. Where did you first meet, and what did you make of them that day?
Tell me about a small mistake that snowballed. What was the mistake, and how far did it get before someone caught it?
What's the worst travel delay you've ever sat through? Where were you stuck, and how did you pass the time?
What was the first concert or show you ever went to? Who took you, and what do you remember about the room?
Tell me about a time something broke at home at a bad moment. What gave out, and who ended up dealing with it?
Tell me about a surprise you planned, or one that was sprung on you. How was it kept secret, and what happened at the reveal?
Tell me about a time you were spectacularly late. What were you late for, and what excuse did you give?
Tell me about one holiday meal you remember better than the others. Who was at the table, and what made that year different?
What's the first thing you ever cooked for other people? How did it come out, and what did they say?
Tell me about a game or match you saw in person. Where were you sitting, and what's the play you remember best?
Tell me about a time an animal outsmarted you: a pet, a pigeon, a raccoon. What did it do, and what did you do about it?
Tell me about your first week in a new city or neighborhood. What did you have to figure out, and where did you eat?
Where did your school take you on trips? Tell me about the one you remember best, and what happened on the bus.
When was the last time you got locked out of somewhere? How did you finally get back in?
What's the best wedding or big party you've ever been to? What made it better than the rest, and how late did you stay?
What's the best thing you ever bought that you absolutely did not need? Tell me about the moment you decided to get it.
When did directions last send you somewhere wrong? Where did you end up, and whose fault was it?
Where's the strangest place you've ever fallen asleep? How did you end up there, and how did you sleep?
Tell me about your first time on a plane or a boat. Where were you headed, and what surprised you about it?
Tell me about a prank that worked, or one that went too far. Who was the target, and how did they take it?
When did the power last go out on you? What were you doing when it happened, and how did you spend the hours after?
Tell me about a group project that nearly fell apart. What was your job, and how did it get finished?
What was your first job? Tell me about the boss, and about one shift you still remember.
What's something you've won: a raffle, a trophy, a bet? Tell me how you won it and what happened to the prize.
Tell me about a time you spoke in front of a crowd. What was the occasion, and what do you remember about the first minute?
Tell me about the worst haircut you've ever had. How did you know it was no good, and how long before you fixed it?
What's the best road trip you've taken? Who was in the car, and what was the best stop along the way?
What's something a kid once said that you've never forgotten? Who was the kid, and how did the adults react?
Tell me about a whole day you spent outside. Where were you, and what shape were you in by the end of it?
Who's someone you ran into after years of not seeing them? Where were you, and what did you two talk about?
Tell me about something you fixed with no idea what you were doing. What was broken, and has it broken again since?
Tell me about your first meal in a place you'd never been before. Where were you, and how did you decide what to order?
What's the longest you've ever waited in a line? What was at the end of it, and was it worth it?
Tell me about a time you got caught in rain or snow. Where were you headed, and what did you look like when you arrived?
Tell me about a celebration that almost didn't happen. What nearly stopped it, and who rescued it?
Tell me about an order or delivery that showed up wrong. What did you ask for, what arrived, and what did you do about it?
Tell me about going back to a place that had changed since you last saw it. What was different, and what did you miss?

“Priya's train stopped between stations, and the lights went out.” What stopped it, and what does she do next?
“Nobody had opened the shop on the corner for ten years, until Dolores did this morning.” Who is Dolores, and what is she selling?
“Biscuit trotted home carrying a wallet that belonged to nobody in the house.” Whose wallet is it, and where did Biscuit find it?
“At midnight, Ingrid heard the piano next door start playing again.” Who's playing, and why only at midnight?
“The letter in Grace's mailbox was addressed to someone who had never lived there.” Who was it meant for, and what does Grace do with it?
“Halfway up the mountain, Rafael the guide admitted he had never been this way before.” Why did he take the job, and how does the group get down?
“The power came back on, but only in one house on the street.” What's different about that house, and what do the neighbors do about it?
“Maryanne opened the top drawer of the old desk, and found a carefully folded note.” Who wrote it, and what did it say?
“Captain Ruiz's ferry left on time, with one passenger too many.” Who is the extra passenger, and where are they trying to go?
“Since the storm, the town's clocks all showed different times.” What did the storm do to them, and how does anyone get anywhere on time?
“Chef Marguerite tasted the soup and went very quiet.” What's in the soup, and what does she do about it?
“Anton's lost suitcase turned up on his doorstep, three years late.” Where has it been, and what's in it now?
“The elevator opened onto a floor that wasn't on the panel, and Rosa stepped out.” What's on that floor, and who does she meet there?
“On the last day of school, Ms. Abara handed back a test nobody remembered taking.” What was the test on, and how did everyone do?
“Mrs. Lindqvist's new tenant paid a year's rent in coins.” Where did the coins come from, and what does the tenant do all day?
“Imani's radio switched itself on in the middle of the night.” What was it playing, and who was it for?
“Beatrice noticed that two guests at the wedding were wearing the same disguise.” Who are they hiding from, and what does Beatrice do?
“Sanjay's map ended at the river, but the footprints did not.” Who left the footprints, and where do they lead?
“When the tide went out, there was a door in the sand.” What's behind the door, and who finds out first?
“Wanda, the babysitter, arrived an hour before anyone had called her.” How did she know, and what does she know that the family doesn't?
“The last bus of the night was not on any schedule.” Where does it go, and who rides it?
“The orchestra began a piece that was not in the program.” Whose idea was it, and how does the audience take it?
“Jerome opened the fridge and found everything rearranged.” Who rearranged it, and what's the new system?
“Edith, the lighthouse keeper, had not written in the log for nine days.” What happened on the first day, and what will her next entry say?
“Fatima's bakery sold out before it opened.” Who bought everything, and what's it all for?

Tell the story that ends this way: The train left on time, and so, for once, did they.
Tell the story that ends this way: The recipe is still taped inside the cupboard door.
